title: Mapping property of the normalized unit into a quotient Roos limit
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative Noetherian ring, $J$ an ideal, and $U$ an object of the coefficient-sized pro-etale site. Let $R$ be the completed coefficient sheaf restricted to $U$, $q_n:R\to B_n$ its actual projections, and $M\in D(R)$ [def-sfb-adic-residue-lift-comparisons]. Use the normalized scalar adjunctions $F_n\dashv G_n$ and the tower $T_n=G_nF_nM$ with counit-transpose successors [lem-sfb-adic-residue-adjoint-tower]. Let $c$ be any homotopy-limit cone over this specified tower [def-weil-derived-limit]. Suppose $a:M\to c.pt$ satisfies $c_n\circ a=\eta_{n,M}$ for every $n\geq0$. For every $L\in D(R)$ locally complete for $\ker(q_0)$ [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete], precomposition with $a$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(c.pt,L)\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,L)$. No assertion about completeness of $c.pt$ or any Cech model is included.

proof.text: Construct an augmented Cech model for the actual finite-type residue kernel. A finite quotient complex restricted to R is complete: nilpotent localization is zero, scalar restriction preserves the sectionwise completeness condition, and complete elements form an ideal containing the completed images of J. The Lean private helpers prove nilpotent localization directly from its sequential-colimit definition.

The Cech mapping bijection implies closure of complete objects under any existing countable product: extend every projection through the unit, construct a retraction, and use uniqueness to obtain its other inverse identity. Apply exact derived restriction and exact internal Hom to the supplied Roos triangle. Both product terms are complete, so its first object c.pt is complete.

Let eta:M to P be the Cech reflector unit. For every finite quotient target N, its restricted complex is complete. Conjugating the Cech Hom bijection with the normalized scalar adjunction proves that precomposition with F_n(eta) is bijective on every outgoing Hom set. Coyoneda proves F_n(eta) invertible.

Factor a uniquely as eta followed by f:P to c.pt. The scalar transpose p:F_0(c.pt) to F_0(M) of the residue leg is invertible by the finite-projection calculation. Adjoint naturality and ha(0) give F_0(a) followed by p equal to identity. Thus F_0(a), and then F_0(f), are invertible.

The universal scalar extension inherits its exact shift structure from the existing cochain model via uniqueness of left derived functors. Complete objects are closed under cones, as their internal-Hom tests and restrictions are exact. Complete a distinguished triangle on f; its third object Q is complete and F_0(Q) is zero. The independent Koszul residue-zero theorem makes Q zero, hence f invertible.

For every complete L, compose the bijection Hom(P,L) to Hom(M,L) with precomposition by the isomorphism f:P to c.pt. Its forward function is precomposition by a. In Lean injectivity cancels f and uses reflector uniqueness; surjectivity extends a given map through eta and precomposes that extension with inverse f.

theorem adicResidueQuotientUnit_universal
    (X : Scheme.{u}) {A : Type (max v (u + 1))} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (J : Ideal A) (U : coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X)
    (M : AdicResidueLocalDerived.{u, v} X J U)
    (c : Cone (adicResidueAdjointTower.{u, v} X J U M))
    (hc : Pretriangulated.IsHomotopyLimit c) (a : M ⟶ c.pt)
    (ha : ∀ n : ℕ, a ≫ c.π.app (op n) =
      (adicResidueScalarAdjunction.{u, v} X J U n).unit.app M) :
    ∀ L : AdicResidueLocalDerived.{u, v} X J U,
      IsComplete (adicResidueLocalProjection.{u, v} X J U 0) L →
        Function.Bijective (fun f : c.pt ⟶ L ↦ a ≫ f)
